label: deceptive
text: Soft bamboo bath towels. Made from 100% bamboo, an eco-friendly, renewable fiber.
source: FTC v. Kohl's and Walmart (2022): rayon textiles marketed as bamboo with environmental benefits; $5.5M in penalties.

label: deceptive
text: Our bamboo baby blanket is naturally antibacterial and made from bamboo grown without pesticides.
source: FTC bamboo textile cases (2010, Sears, Kmart, Amazon and others; 2013 follow-ups): bamboo rayon cannot claim bamboo's natural properties.

label: deceptive
text: Our plastic bags are 100% biodegradable. Just toss them in the trash and they break down.
source: FTC biodegradable plastics cases (2013-2016, e.g. ECM BioFilms, Clear Choice Housewares): unqualified biodegradable claims for landfilled plastics.

label: deceptive
text: Disposable paper plates: biodegradable and better for the environment.
source: FTC v. Kmart / American Fare (2009): biodegradable claim for paper plates that are usually landfilled.

label: deceptive
text: Moist bath wipes: biodegradable and septic safe, so you can feel good about every use.
source: FTC v. Tender Corp. (2009): biodegradable claim for wipes without competent evidence.

label: deceptive
text: Single-serve coffee pods. Have it your way, then recycle it! Our pods are recyclable.
source: Keurig 'recyclable' pod claims: Canada Competition Bureau settlement (2022, C$3M) and U.S. class action settlement (2022, $10M); not accepted by most municipal programs.

label: deceptive
text: Zero VOC interior paint. Safe for your family and the planet.
source: FTC v. Sherwin-Williams, Benjamin Moore and others (2015): 'zero VOC' claims while colorants added VOCs.

label: deceptive
text: Look for the Green Promise seal on our paints, our mark of environmental responsibility.
source: FTC v. Benjamin Moore (2015): company-created 'Green Promise' seal implied independent certification.

label: deceptive
text: Our crib mattresses carry the Green Safety Shield seal and are certified organic and non-toxic.
source: FTC v. Moonlight Slumber (2017): self-created seal and unsupported organic claims.

label: deceptive
text: Fly CO2ZERO: offset the emissions of your flight and travel carbon neutral.
source: Fossielvrij NL v. KLM, Amsterdam District Court (2024): offset and 'responsible flying' claims found misleading.

label: deceptive
text: This shampoo is climate neutral: we compensate all of its CO2 emissions through certified forest projects.
source: EU Directive 2024/825: offset-based climate neutral product claims banned from 27 September 2026.

label: deceptive
text: Strong trash bags made with 50% ocean plastic.
source: ACCC v. Clorox Australia (2024, A$8.25M penalty): 'ocean plastic' was plastic collected up to 50km inland, not from the ocean.

label: deceptive
text: Our Conscious collection: sustainable fashion that is better for the planet.
source: Norwegian Consumer Authority on H&M Conscious (2019) and EU Directive 2024/825 ban on generic environmental claims.

label: deceptive
text: Eco-friendly dish soap. Earth-safe and green.
source: FTC Green Guides 16 CFR 260.4: unqualified general environmental benefit claims.

label: compliant
text: Shipping box made from 70% recycled paper fiber by weight.
source: Green Guides 260.13: recycled content stated as a percentage.

label: compliant
text: Plastic bottle: recyclable in the few communities that collect #5 plastics. Check with your local program; it may not be accepted in your area.
source: Green Guides 260.12: qualified recyclable claim where facilities are limited.

label: compliant
text: This bag is compostable in industrial composting facilities, which may not exist in your area. Not suitable for home composting. Certified to ASTM D6400 by BPI.
source: Green Guides 260.7: qualified compostable claim disclosing facility availability.

label: compliant
text: New bottle design uses 20% less plastic than our previous 32 oz bottle.
source: Green Guides 260.17 and 260.3: source reduction with amount and basis of comparison.

label: compliant
text: Made with 100% organic cotton, certified by the Global Organic Textile Standard (GOTS), license number CU 123456.
source: Specific, third-party-certified material claim (Green Guides 260.6 for certifications).

label: compliant
text: Our factory runs on 60% solar power generated on site; the rest comes from the regional grid.
source: Green Guides 260.15: renewable energy claim stating the source and share.

label: compliant
text: Refill pouches available: return the empty glass bottle to any of our stores and we refill it for free.
source: Green Guides 260.14: refillable claim backed by a refill system.

label: compliant
text: Packaging: cardboard box contains 85% recycled fibre, certified by FSC Recycled (licence FSC-C000000).
source: Specific, certified recycled-content claim permitted under EU 2024/825.
